correctness.rationale: For successive tangent angular gaps d, local area excess is r(theta)^2 d^3/24+O(d^4), perimeter excess r(theta)d^3/12+O(d^4), uniformly on the exponentially likely good-gap event. One-/two-point Poisson Palm covariance of cubic gap rewards gives local coefficient 720-108-108=504 times integral(wv). A truncated independent-block Lyapunov argument yields joint CLT with λ^(5/2) scaling; O(Σd^4) error is L2-negligible. Substituting w=r²/24 and r/12 gives Σ entries 7/8∫r4, 7/4∫r³, 7/2∫r²; determinant is 49/16[(∫r4)(∫r2)-(∫r3)²], zero iff r is constant, equivalent to h=R+a cosθ+b sinθ and thus a translated disk. Independently recomputed 504 and determinant cancellation at constant r.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge precise model is Poisson sampling of EXACT supporting tangent normals, with conditional good gaps, and simultaneous area/perimeter fluctuations. Prior Bakó-Szabó-Fodor bounds mean-width variance for random offset hyperplanes, while Calka-Demichel-Enriquez and Hug-Schneider analyze Poisson-Voronoi/offset hyperplanes; they do not present this fixed-support cubic-gap covariance, Gaussian joint law or disk-rigidity determinant. Other published tangent-polygon results concern finite fixed-n heavy area tails, a different scaling regime.
residual_risks: A classic circular-spacing process or stochastic-geometry CLT may already contain a reformulation of the exact joint covariance.
Conditional good-gap model excludes heavy-tail unbounded polygon events; no unconditional area moments or fixed-sample coefficient claimed.

value.rationale: Provides a concrete geometric statistical test of circularity in the high-intensity limit: separate Gaussian marginals cannot identify disk shape, but singularity of their joint covariance does. The explicit curvature moment matrix and condition of equality are natural shape invariants, not an unmotivated numerical constant.

limitations: Smooth C4 strictly convex with strictly positive curvature radius, and conditioning on all angle gaps <=π/2.
No fixed-n or unconditioned-moment assertion; no Berry-Esseen bound.
